items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-CHS-25-004, Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) Funding and Directed Growth Update
notes:
Barb Cardow, Director of Children's Services provided a presentation related to CSD-CHS-25-004, Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) Funding and Directed Growth Update. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. 

B. Cardow highlighted that there are 2,656 new CWELCC childcare spaces have been created in the Region and are planning on creating an additional 1,480 spaces before the end of 2026. She explained that the Ministry of Education required all Service System Managers (SSMs) to develop plans to prioritize new spaces where the needs for affordable childcare are highest. Staff prioritized areas that would better serve low-income families. CWELCC spaces are allocated through transparent Requests for Proposals using consistent criteria such as inclusion of priority families, financial viability, location, and quality. She explained that there is no guarantee of CWELCC funding and that the federal and provincial funding is fully committed and that there is a fixed number of new CWELCC spaces and no indication of more CWELCC spaces in the future. She agreed that more affordable childcare spaces are needed and staff continue to advocate for more spaces and more funding.

Responding to the Committee, B. Cardow clarified that for-profit childcare operators can transition to become non-for-profit and the transition process can take approximately three months. She further clarified that that all operators using CWELCC funding must charge $22.00 per day. The difference between for-profit and non-for-profit operators is that the for-profit operators can use the 7% funding in any manner they choose whereas non-for-profit must commit that revenue back into CWELCC initiatives.

In response to the Committee, B. Cardow explained that the Breslau childcare spaces are all being allocated to non-for-profit and there is a finite amount of spaces based on the guidelines related to the CWELCC program and all spaces must be the CWELCC set amount of $22 per day. Staff were not provided the reasoning behind the provincial relocation of spaces and shift to the 90% non-for-profit spaces. The federal and provincial government are working on the details related to $10.00 a day childcare program and the Regional funding is based on upper level governments determine for allocation.

The Committee discussed the importance of advocacy to the federal and provincial government for increased funding to better assist the approximately 14,000 families on the Regional childcare waitlist.

C. James indicated that she will be crafting a motion for Council to consider at the Council meeting on December 17, 2025.

Received for information.
